title: Golden Signals — API
description: Traffic/error/latency/saturation for openlex-api. Latency, generic traffic, and error-rate still have no data source (see the panel notes) — Phase 3 (observability app instrumentation) added OTel traces and log/trace correlation but deliberately did not add an OTel metrics pipeline; see the panel text for exactly what's missing and why.

panels.title: Traffic — still not instrumented (checked again post-Phase-3)

options.content: **Traffic, error-rate, and p50/p95/p99 latency panels remain blocked after the Phase 3 app-instrumentation pass.** Re-verified directly against openlex-api's live `/metrics` output: it exports only `openlex_query_requests_total` and `openlex_query_quota_exceeded_total` (both `prometheus_client` Counters labeled `tier` only, see `apps/api/src/openlex_api/quota.py`) plus the default Python process/GC metrics — still no per-route HTTP request counter, no error-status breakdown, and no request-duration histogram. Phase 3 added `opentelemetry-instrumentation-fastapi` (see `apps/api/src/openlex_api/telemetry.py`), which *internally* calls `meter.create_histogram(...)` for `http.server.duration` — but that instrument is bound to whatever `MeterProvider` is globally registered, and this codebase never calls `opentelemetry.metrics.set_meter_provider(...)`, so it resolves to the OTel SDK's default no-op `ProxyMeterProvider`: the histogram silently records into nothing. Phase 3 only wired **traces** (spans in Tempo/Jaeger) and the logging bridge, not an OTel **metrics** pipeline. Tier/quota traffic (not generic HTTP traffic) is visible on the separate **Tier & Quota** dashboard. To unblock these panels, a future task needs to either (a) add a real OTel metrics pipeline — a `MeterProvider` + `PeriodicExportingMetricReader` wired to an OTLP or Prometheus exporter, registered via `set_meter_provider` before `FastAPIInstrumentor.instrument_app()` runs — or (b) add `prometheus-fastapi-instrumentator` (or hand-rolled `Histogram`/`Counter` middleware) directly exporting via the existing `/metrics` endpoint. Neither exists yet. Only CPU/memory saturation (below) can be shown for openlex-api today, from cAdvisor data.

panels.title: Error rate — still not instrumented (checked again post-Phase-3)

options.content: **No HTTP-level error-rate metric exists today, confirmed after Phase 3.** There is no per-status-code request counter anywhere in `apps/api` (grepped for `Histogram`/`Counter` from `prometheus_client` — only `quota.py`'s two tier-labeled counters exist, neither carries `status_code`). Traces do carry `http.status_code` per-request (visible in Tempo/Jaeger), but that's not the same as an aggregable error-rate metric for alerting/dashboards. Requires: an OTel metrics pipeline (`MeterProvider` + exporter) or `prometheus-fastapi-instrumentator` — not yet added.

panels.title: p50/p95/p99 latency — still not instrumented (checked again post-Phase-3)

options.content: **No latency metric exists today, confirmed after Phase 3.** `opentelemetry-instrumentation-fastapi`'s internal duration histogram is a no-op here because no `MeterProvider` was ever registered (`opentelemetry.metrics.set_meter_provider` is never called in this codebase — verified by reading the installed `opentelemetry-instrumentation-asgi` source, which creates the histogram via `self.meter.create_histogram(...)` against whatever provider `get_meter()` resolves to, i.e. the SDK's default no-op `ProxyMeterProvider`). Per-request latency *is* visible span-by-span in Tempo/Jaeger, but there's no aggregated p50/p95/p99 metric for a dashboard panel. Requires: a real OTel metrics pipeline (`MeterProvider` + `PeriodicExportingMetricReader` + OTLP/Prometheus exporter, registered before `FastAPIInstrumentor.instrument_app()` runs) or `prometheus-fastapi-instrumentator` — not yet added.
